post.description:
Check which data connectors are configured for this artist and return
their credential status.

This endpoint validates that the required environment variables are set
for each connector.  It does NOT make real API calls — it only confirms
that the credentials are present and the connector is ready to use.

For connectors that are not yet configured, use the statement file upload
workflow: POST /artists/{artist_id}/statements/upload

get.description:
Return an ML-derived catalog health score (0–100) and grade for the artist.

Combines metadata completeness, payment regularity, anomaly density,
recovery rate, and earnings accuracy into a single composite score.

post.description:
Use a linear-regression trend model to forecast the artist's earnings for
the next *horizon_days* days.

Set ``by_category=true`` to receive a per-event-type breakdown.

get.description:
Return statute-of-limitations classification for all open anomalies.

Each anomaly is classified as EXPIRED, URGENT (<90 days), AT_RISK
(90–180 days), or OK (>180 days remaining), sorted most-urgent first.
Also returns an overall SOL exposure summary.

Compare the artist's actual payment rates against industry benchmarks.

Returns a full report including per-event-type comparisons, estimated
underpayment amounts, and a tier classification
(ABOVE_MARKET, AT_MARKET, BELOW_MARKET, CRITICAL).

Return audit-rights eligibility for all contracts.

Contracts are ranked by estimated potential recovery and eligibility
status (NEVER_AUDITED, ELIGIBLE, ELIGIBLE_SOON, NOT_YET_ELIGIBLE).

Return recoupment position and any discrepancy flags for all contracts
with advance/recoupment provisions.

Flags RECOUPMENT_DISCREPANCY when the calculated balance differs from
the counterparty-reported balance, and EXCESS_RECOUPMENT when more than
the advance has been recouped.

Return a unified, prioritised action queue for the artist.

Merges open anomalies and in-flight claims into a single ranked list,
scoring each item by (estimated_recoverable × confidence × urgency) / age.
The artist (or their representative) should work through this list
top-to-bottom to maximise recovery.

post.description:
Step 1 of the MFA flow.

Validates the artist's identity details, creates a verification session,
and dispatches a 6-digit OTP to both the provided phone number and email
address.

In **development** environments (``XR7_ENV`` ≠ ``production``), the
OTPs are also returned in the response body under ``dev_phone_otp`` and
``dev_email_otp`` so that local testing requires no external credentials.
These fields are **absent** in production.

Step 2 of the MFA flow.

Both the phone OTP and email OTP must be correct.  On success, a
short-lived estimate token is returned.  This token must be presented
to ``POST /widget/estimate`` to retrieve the royalty estimate.

Step 3 of the MFA flow.

Presents the estimate token obtained from ``POST /widget/verify`` along
with optional career profile information.  Saves a lead record to the
database, emails the estimate results to the artist, and returns the
full royalty owed estimate.

Mark a lead as "claimed" when the artist clicks the recovery CTA.

The ``lead_id`` returned by ``POST /widget/estimate`` is required.
Idempotent — calling this multiple times on the same lead is safe.

get.description:
Return all widget leads in reverse-chronological order.

Requires the ``X-Admin-Key`` request header to equal the
``WIDGET_ADMIN_KEY`` environment variable.

schema.title: Response List Leads Widget Leads Get

get.description:
Return the complete list of explicitly supported royalty statement CSV
formats, grouped by type (distributor, PRO, DSP, generic).

For each format the response includes:
- ``name`` — human-readable distributor/PRO name
- ``type`` — ``"distributor"`` | ``"pro"`` | ``"dsp"`` | ``"generic"``
- ``key_columns`` — representative column headers from that format's CSV
- ``description`` — how to obtain the file and what it covers

Any CSV that does not match an explicit format is handled by the
``"generic"`` fallback, which recognises any file with recognisable date,
source, quantity, and amount columns.  This covers distributors such as
Songtradr, Vydia, AWAL, Symphonic, INgrooves, Believe, Kobalt, and others.

schema.title: Response Supported Formats Ingestion Supported Formats Get

post.description:
Upload a royalty statement CSV and ingest it into the database.

Supported formats are automatically detected from the column headers:
**DistroKid**, **TuneCore**, **CD Baby**, **ASCAP**, **BMI**,
**Spotify for Artists**, and a **generic** fallback for any CSV with
recognisable date / amount / quantity columns.

After ingestion, anomaly detection is run automatically so that any
under-payment issues are immediately flagged.

Returns a :class:`~XR7.models.statement.Statement` record summarising
what was parsed and saved.

**Requires prior acceptance of the Artist Recovery Services Agreement.**
Call ``GET /terms`` to read the agreement and
``POST /artists/{artist_id}/terms/accept`` to accept it.  This endpoint
returns HTTP 403 until the artist has agreed to the terms.
Upload and process a batch of statement CSV files in a single request.

post.description:
Register an artist in the Celero Commerce Customer Vault.

Creates a new vault record with the artist's contact details.  The
returned ``celero_customer_vault_id`` is stored on the Artist and used
for all subsequent charges and disbursements.

The artist's actual payment credentials (card number / bank account)
are added separately using Celero's **Collect.js** or **Collect Checkout**
hosted form — XR7 never handles raw payment data.

Requires ``CELERO_SECURITY_KEY`` to be configured.

get.description:
Return the Celero Commerce integration status for an artist.

Shows whether the artist has been registered in the Celero vault and
a summary of their transaction history.

put.description: Update an artist's contact details in the Celero Customer Vault.

post.description:
Charge the artist's Celero-vaulted payment method for XR7's
10% contingency fee on a reconciled claim.

The claim must be in ``PAID`` status with a ``recovered_amount`` set.
The charge amount is calculated as ``recovered_amount × 10%``.

Requires:
- The artist to be registered with Celero (``celero_customer_vault_id`` set).
- ``CELERO_SECURITY_KEY`` to be configured.

Disburse the artist's net recovery amount via ACH credit through Celero.

The ``amount`` should be the gross recovery minus XR7's contingency
fee.  Celero will credit the artist's bank account stored in their vault.

Requires:
- The artist to have a bank account on file in their Celero vault.
- Celero ACH payout capability to be enabled on the XR7 merchant account.
- ``CELERO_SECURITY_KEY`` to be configured.

Issue a partial or full refund for a previous CHARGE transaction.

If ``amount`` is omitted, the full transaction amount is refunded.

Void an unsettled CHARGE transaction (typically same-day).

Use ``refund`` for transactions that have already settled.

post.description:
Receive and process real-time event notifications from Celero Commerce.

Configure this URL in the Celero merchant dashboard:
  Settings → Webhooks → Add Endpoint → ``https://your-domain/celero/webhook``

Supported events: ``transaction.approved``, ``transaction.declined``,
``transaction.void``, ``transaction.refund``, ``disbursement.settled``,
``disbursement.failed``.

Every request is validated against the HMAC-SHA256 signature in the
``X-Celero-Signature`` header using ``CELERO_WEBHOOK_SECRET``.

get.description: Serve the standalone artist recovery dashboard UI page.

Return the artist's full recovery dashboard.

**leakage_discovered**
- ``total_anomalies`` — total number of anomalies detected
- ``total_estimated_recoverable`` — sum of estimated recoverable amounts
- ``by_category`` — breakdown by revenue category (ROYALTY, TOURING, etc.)
- ``by_severity`` — breakdown by severity (LOW / MEDIUM / HIGH / CRITICAL)
- ``recent_discoveries`` — last 10 newly detected anomalies

**in_pursuit**
- ``active_claim_count`` — number of open claims
- ``total_amount_in_pursuit`` — total dollar value of active claims
- ``total_gross_recovered`` — total recovered across all closed/paid claims
- ``total_net_recovered`` — gross minus XR7 contingency fees

**recovered_and_deposited**
- ``total_deposited`` — sum of all Celero disbursements received
- ``deposits`` — per-deposit log with Celero transaction IDs

**balance_still_pursuing**
- ``balance_still_pursuing`` — the key number: money we are still chasing
- ``total_pending_deposit`` — approved but not yet ACH-settled

**deadlines**
- ``expired_count`` — anomalies whose SOL window has already closed
- ``urgent_count`` — anomalies with <90 days remaining on their SOL window
- ``at_risk_count`` — anomalies with 90–180 days remaining
- ``top_urgent_items`` — up to 5 most time-sensitive anomalies with days_remaining

**priority_actions**
- ``top_10_actions`` — ranked action items (anomalies + claims) by ROI × urgency
- ``total_open_items`` — total items in the priority queue

**catalog_health**
- ``health_score`` — ML composite score 0–100
- ``grade`` — letter grade A–F
- ``signals`` — per-signal breakdown (metadata, payment regularity, etc.)
- ``recommendations`` — list of actionable improvement suggestions

**earnings_trend**
- ``trend`` — GROWING / FLAT / DECLINING / INSUFFICIENT_DATA
- ``predicted_total`` — predicted earnings over next 90 days
- ``predicted_low`` / ``predicted_high`` — 95% confidence interval

**activity_feed**
- Up to 50 timestamped events: leakage discoveries, claim updates,
  and payment deposits, newest first.

Return the current Artist Recovery Services Agreement text, version
identifier, and SHA-256 hash.

The client should render the full ``text`` field for the artist to read
before presenting the acceptance checkbox.  The ``version`` and ``sha256``
values must be echoed back verbatim in POST /artists/{id}/terms/accept.

post.description:
Record the artist's acceptance of the current Artist Recovery Services
Agreement.

This endpoint:
1. Verifies the artist exists.
2. Verifies the version the artist was shown matches the live version
   (stale-page protection).
3. Verifies the ``agreed`` flag is ``true`` — a bare form POST cannot
   accidentally create an acceptance record.
4. Persists an immutable TermsAcceptance row with server-set timestamp,
   IP address, and User-Agent string.

Submitting again after the artist has already accepted the current version
is idempotent — the existing acceptance record is returned without creating
a duplicate.

get.description:
Return whether the artist has accepted the current version of the
Artist Recovery Services Agreement.

``accepted`` is ``True`` only if there is an acceptance record for the
*current* live version.  If the terms were updated since the artist last
agreed, ``accepted`` will be ``False`` and ``pending_version`` will
indicate the version the artist needs to accept.

get.description:
Return the platform readiness status for every integration point.

Operators can call this endpoint to see exactly which connectors are
configured (credentials present) vs. which require additional setup.

``ready`` is ``True`` only when the core platform components are
functional.  Individual connector status reflects whether the required
environment variables are set — it does NOT make real network connections.

CeleroChargeRequest.description: Charge the artist's Celero vault for a specific claim's contingency fee.

Disburse a net recovery amount to the artist via ACH.

``amount`` is the net amount in USD after XR7's fee has been deducted.
``claim_id`` is optional — omit for manual / ad-hoc disbursements.

CeleroRegisterRequest.title: CeleroRegisterRequest
CeleroRegisterRequest.description:
Information needed to create an artist as a Celero customer.

Card / bank account details are collected separately via Celero's
hosted Collect.js form and never pass through XR7 servers.

TermsAcceptRequest.title: TermsAcceptRequest
TermsAcceptRequest.description:
Body for POST /artists/{artist_id}/terms/accept.

``terms_version`` must match the version the server returns from
GET /terms.  This prevents a client that cached an old version of the
T&C from accidentally accepting stale terms.
